as_told.title: Schoch and Hancock: the Sphinx as an homage to Leo

plain: A researcher named Randall Carlson, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, recalls that two writers, Robert Bauval and Graham Hancock, tried to date the Great Sphinx at Giza in Egypt by the stars. Their idea, as he tells it, was to work out when the sunrise on the spring equinox, the day each year when day and night are equal, would have lined up with where the Sphinx is looking, which he puts at about 10,500 BC. If true, it would make the Sphinx far older than it is usually thought to be.
